detail.body:
## Motivation

Co-author: @Shunkangz

Connect GLM DSA/MTP serving to page-sharded KV caches so prefill, P/D transfer and CPU HiCache preserve the same ownership for target/draft latent KV and DSA indexer keys/scales.

## Dependencies and review scope

Base: upstream main `5987ec82ed`. Current head: `346068aaa329cf1692fbb6031f60469fdac77dcb`.

DSA attention/indexer support (#44280), MTP pool/scratch support (#40929), and the control-plane/pool/basic-PD prerequisites are already merged.

The remaining unmerged prerequisite is **#43778**, pinned at `6d1e510b2429a36fe499943ff075472d995d8457`. Its three implementation commits are rebased onto this main base with Shunkang's author attribution preserved. The dependency snapshot is `152e93348ad825449c484fbee2068fc614116c67`.

**Review the integration increment:** https://github.com/HZY-Wade/sglang/compare/codex/kvshard-glm-dependencies-20261026-clean...codex/kvshard-dsa-hicache

GitHub's main-based Files changed view also includes #43778. **Rust support is separate in #46445**; this PR contains no Rust implementation and selects Python for sharded launches when the tree backend is unset.

## Modifications

- Select page-sharded DSA target and single-layer GLM NextN draft pools. Validate matching cache geometry and budget latent/indexer scratch for both runners.
- Preserve the shared sender lifecycle. Pair source/destination DSA pages before owner filtering, transfer every owner's target/draft state, retain empty-final-chunk completion, and account for physical transfer bytes.
- Compose a standalone sharded allocation facade with native host pools. Reuse HybridCacheController and L2TransferEngine; resolve owner-local indices through existing preparation hooks before the H2D start event. Preserve logical queue indices and ACK counts.
- Scope scratch bookkeeping to sharding, cache the controller's sharding flag, retain ordinary transfer descriptor builders, and remove the redundant FULL eviction retry.
- Pass `start_owner` to backups only when the tree node has a shard owner. Preserve owner zero and the non-sharded controller's existing call signature.
- Add a four-GPU GLM P2/D2 E2E with CP2, EAGLE MTP and CPU HiCache. Use fabric NVLink with Mooncake's exportable KV allocator, matching the existing P2/D2 test on the same GB300 runner. CPU tests follow the registered `CustomTestCase` convention.

Supported configuration: CUDA PD-prefill, interleave CP > 1, PP1, TRTLLM DSA prefill/decode, FP8 E4M3/page64, Mooncake, and uncompressed index_kpool=1. Optional MTP is single-layer GLM NextN EAGLE with topk=1. CPU HiCache uses cache mode, kernel I/O and layer_first/page_first. L3, external linkers, DSA layer splitting, HiSparse and two-batch overlap are outside this combination. Decode remains unsharded.

[Configuration requirements, paired launch example and validation guidance](https://github.com/HZY-Wade/sglang/blob/codex/kvshard-dsa-hicache/docs/docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.mdx#glm-dsa-kv-sharding-with-cpu-hicache)

## Accuracy Tests

- Runtime regression on `f01f901a6a` (runtime source unchanged by the following documentation/fixture commits): **200 tests and 140 subtests passed**, 2 skipped, 1 deselected. This covers owner-aware PD transfer, allocator/rotation invariants, scratch sizing, scheduler admission, host-transfer dispatch, launch compatibility and controller event ordering.
- Both new CPU test files also pass when executed directly with fail-fast, as CI invokes them: 4 PD transfer tests and 2 controller tests.
- The unsharded host-prefix backup setup independently reproduces the published head's `unexpected keyword argument 'start_owner'` failure and passes with `8620dbdaa1`.
- Local CPU runs bypass only the Mac Torch/MPS version preflight. A platform-specific NPU host-pool test is deselected because the local host-memory reserve cannot be met; GPU-dependent tests are skipped. These runs do not validate CUDA/NCCL or physical host transfers.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass. Mintlify 4.2.559 reports no broken links with anchor/redirect checks. Both documented launch commands pass the CLI parser and their shell block passes `bash -n`.

### Hardware E2E status

**Passed on current head `346068aaa329cf1692fbb6031f60469fdac77dcb`, Base attempt 2.**

- [Four-GB300 hardware job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354128180/job/121958752142): `test_dsa_glm52_pd_kv_shard_hicache.py` actually ran and passed, with a 273-second suite duration. The test method completed with `Ran 1 test ... OK`; this was not a collection-only or skipped result.
- The test retains P2/D2, CP2, EAGLE MTP and all cold/device-hit/host-reloaded answer, speculative-verification, host-hit and rank-specific H2D assertions. Two 6,144-token pressure requests exceed the 8,192 logical GPU slots while fitting with the target prefix in the larger host cache.
- [CPU partition 17](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354128180/job/121958700456): all 52 files passed, including `test_decode_hicache_l2.py` (36 seconds), which previously exposed the non-sharded backup signature regression.
- The existing AARCH64 P2/D2 accuracy test also passed in the same GB300 job (89 seconds). This fixture uses its supported fabric configuration: `MC_FORCE_MNNVL=true` and `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=NVLINK`. The NVLink allocator supplies exportable KV buffers; the runner's wheel does not provide `nvlink_intra`.

The launch example has separate prefill/decode commands with one option per line, addressing review comment 4379290548. CLI arguments are unchanged; both examples match the E2E transport settings. Shell syntax, CLI parsing, allocator selection equivalence, pre-commit and Mintlify anchor/link checks pass.

The separate existing [GLM-5.2 layer-split accuracy rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354126514/job/122014411774) **passed at 0.9422632794457275**, above the unchanged **0.935** GSM8K threshold; the full job passed 2/2 test files. The previous attempt scored 0.9345650500384911. Both attempts tested merge `e79b8b8c52735038eb60edcacff7a3e6f24ea69e` with KV sharding disabled, and no code or threshold changes were made between them. The successful rerun does not establish the cause of the score variation.

On current head, [Base attempt 3](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354128180/attempts/3) and [Extra attempt 3](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40354126514/attempts/3) are both successful. Arm64 and Xeon retain separately investigated failures in unchanged CPU-operator/parser paths; the complete platform matrix is not all green.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**A controlled production replay is still pending; no throughput or latency speedup is claimed.**

For the requested comparison, use the same model revision, hardware, runtime, P/D topology, memory budget, request order, concurrency and warm-up policy. Report device/host hit tokens, TTFT percentiles, throughput, peak memory and answer correctness for replicated/deduplicated KV and KV sharding. CPU unit-test counts and increased logical capacity are not performance measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and pre-commit checks.
- [x] Focused regression coverage and CI registration.
- [x] Configuration, launch and validation documentation.
- [x] Preserve non-sharded call paths and follow composition/preparation-hook review feedback.
- [x] Pass the corrected full-model P/D + MTP + HiCache E2E on hardware.
- [ ] Provide controlled production accuracy/performance replay results.
- [x] Pass the separate GLM layer-split accuracy evaluation at the unchanged 0.935 threshold.
- [ ] Resolve the remaining #43778 dependency and required CI/maintainer approvals.

+## GLM DSA KV sharding with CPU HiCache
+
+On prefill workers, `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` distributes cached pages across
+the attention-CP group. Each owner stores and transfers its target/draft latent
+KV and DSA indexer pages. Optional CPU HiCache retains the same page ownership
+during backup and reload. Decode workers receive complete caches and do not
+enable KV sharding.
+
+Use this combination on Linux with NVIDIA CUDA and hardware supported by the
+TRTLLM DSA backends. The `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` example requires Blackwell GPUs
+with enough memory for both target and draft weights on each side.
+
+| Setting | Supported configuration |
+| --- | --- |
+| Prefill parallelism | Interleave CP greater than one; pipeline parallel size one |
+| Attention and KV | TRTLLM DSA prefill/decode, `fp8_e4m3`, page size 64 |
+| DSA indexer | Uncompressed `index_kpool=1`; no cache layer splitting |
+| P/D transfer | Mooncake, with staging buffers disabled |
+| Optional MTP | GLM DSA single-layer NextN, EAGLE, top-k one |
+| Optional CPU HiCache | `cache` mode, `kernel` I/O, `layer_first` or `page_first` |
+
+KV-sharded serving selects the Python radix tree when no tree backend is
+explicitly configured. L3 storage (including runtime attachment), external cache
+linkers, HiSparse and two-batch overlap are unsupported. Prefill CUDA graphs,
+P-side speculative graphs and generic FlashInfer autotuning are disabled for
+this path. Scratch buffers for target and draft are charged against the KV
+memory budget, so the usable cache capacity also depends on context length.
+
+The following single-host GB300/NVL72 example uses GPUs 0–1 for prefill and 2–3
+for decode. Install the [Mooncake transfer engine](#requirements) first. Both
+workers use fabric NVLink with Mooncake's NVLink allocator, which makes their
+KV buffers exportable. Enabling fabric transport alone does not make ordinary
+CUDA allocations remotely accessible. For other hardware, configure the
+appropriate [RDMA or NVLink transport](#nvlink-transport-configuration).
+
+Run prefill and decode in separate terminals on the same host.
+
+### Prefill worker (GPUs 0–1)
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER=0
+export SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=NVLINK
+export MC_FORCE_MNNVL=true
+
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
+  --trust-remote-code \
+  --tp-size 2 \
+  --context-length 16384 \
+  --max-running-requests 1 \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
+  --page-size 64 \
+  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
+  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm \
+  --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
+  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
+  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
+  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
+  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
+  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
+  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
+  --enable-metrics \
+  --enable-cache-report \
+  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
+  --port 30001 \
+  --nccl-port 29501 \
+  --enable-kv-cache-sharding \
+  --enable-prefill-cp \
+  --attn-cp-size 2 \
+  --cp-strategy interleave \
+  --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
+  --max-total-tokens 4096 \
+  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
+  --hicache-ratio 4 \
+  --hicache-write-policy write_through \
+  --hicache-io-backend kernel \
+  --hicache-mem-layout page_first
+```
+
+### Decode worker (GPUs 2–3)
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER=0
+export SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=NVLINK
+export MC_FORCE_MNNVL=true
+
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
+  --trust-remote-code \
+  --tp-size 2 \
+  --context-length 16384 \
+  --max-running-requests 1 \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
+  --page-size 64 \
+  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
+  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm \
+  --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
+  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
+  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
+  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
+  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
+  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
+  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
+  --enable-metrics \
+  --enable-cache-report \
+  --disaggregation-mode decode \
+  --port 30002 \
+  --nccl-port 29502 \
+  --base-gpu-id 2 \
+  --max-total-tokens 16384 \
+  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1
+```
+
+Connect the two endpoints through the [P/D router](#router-integration).
+To check CPU-cache reuse, repeat a prompt after enough unrelated requests have
+evicted its GPU prefix: `cached_tokens_details.host` and the prefill
+`sglang:load_back_tokens_total` counter must increase. A device-cache hit alone
+does not exercise the host reload path.
+
+When comparing with replicated or deduplicated KV, keep the model revision,
+hardware, P/D topology, memory budget, request order, concurrency and warm-up
+policy fixed. Report device/host cache-hit tokens, TTFT percentiles, throughput,
+peak memory and answer correctness. Additional cache capacity alone does not
+establish a latency or throughput gain; use a representative replay and the
+[benchmarking guide](/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling).
+
 ## Profiling in PD Disaggregation Mode
 
 When you need to profile prefill or decode workers in PD disaggregation mode, please refer to the [Profile In PD Disaggregation Mode](../developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling#profile-in-pd-disaggregation-mode) section in the Benchmark and Profiling guide. Due to torch profiler limitations, prefill and decode workers must be profiled separately using dedicated command-line options.

+"""HiCache host pool for logical-page KV sharding (mem_cache/page_interleave.py).
+
+The host pool is striped exactly like its device pool. Host slots live in the
+same widened logical index space and follow the same placement: logical host
+page ``h`` is owned by rank ``h % N`` and is that rank's local host page
+``h // N``. Host slots come from the device's own owner-classed allocator, and
+every backup / load-back pairs device and host pages of the same owner, so a
+rank's share of any transfer is exactly its own pages. Each shard rank
+therefore moves only its stripe between its own HBM and host memory, all ranks
+in parallel, with no cross-rank traffic.
+
+``size`` stays the per-rank row count (the ratio applied to the per-rank
+device pool), so per-rank host memory matches the unsharded case while the
+logical host capacity grows with the shard group, like the device's.
+"""

+
+from typing import Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.page_interleave import PageInterleavePoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.page_interleave import PageInterleavePlacement
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.base import HostKVCache, synchronized
+
+
+class PageInterleaveHostPool:
+    """Compose owner-classed slots with a native host pool's buffers/transfers.
+
+    The native pool is fully constructed before this allocation facade is
+    installed; its constructor and clear() never dispatch into sharding code.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, host_pool: HostKVCache, placement: PageInterleavePlacement):
+        self.host_pool = host_pool
+        self.placement = placement
+        self.shard_rank = placement.spec.shard_rank
+        self.shard_size = placement.spec.shard_size
+        assert self.page_size == self.placement.spec.page_size, (
+            "the sharded host pool pages must match the device's physical page"
+        )
+        self.clear()
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str):
+        # Layout, buffers, transfer kernels and their lifecycle remain owned by
+        # the concrete native pool. Only slot ownership is managed here.
+        return getattr(object.__getattribute__(self, "host_pool"), name)
+
+    @property
+    def logical_size(self) -> int:
+        return self.size * self.shard_size
+
+    @synchronized
+    def clear(self):
+        # The device's classed allocator over this rank's host rows; like the
+        # device, it leaves local page 0 unused.
+        self._slots = PageInterleavePoolAllocator(
+            size=self.size - self.page_size,
+            physical_page_size=self.page_size,
+            shard_size=self.shard_size,
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device="cpu",
+            kvcache=None,
+            need_sort=False,
+        )
+

+        return self._slots.available_size()
+
+    @synchronized

+            "they back up; pass the first page's owner class"

+
+    @synchronized

+        self._slots.free(indices.cpu())
+        return len(indices)
+
+    def owned_rows(
+        self, host_indices: torch.Tensor, device_indices: torch.Tensor

+        """Narrow a logical (host, device) slot pairing to this rank's pages,
+        as local (host, device) rows. Pairs are owner-matched, so ownership
+        is read off the CPU host slots and the device side is a plain gather:
+        no device-to-host sync."""

+            self.placement.local_index(device_owned),

+## GLM DSA KV sharding with CPU HiCache
+
+On prefill workers, `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` distributes cached pages across
+the attention-CP group. Each owner stores and transfers its target/draft latent
+KV and DSA indexer pages. Optional CPU HiCache retains the same page ownership
+during backup and reload. Decode workers receive complete caches and do not
+enable KV sharding.
+
+Use this combination on Linux with NVIDIA CUDA and hardware supported by the
+TRTLLM DSA backends. The `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` example requires Blackwell GPUs
+with enough memory for both target and draft weights on each side.
+
+| Setting | Supported configuration |
+| --- | --- |
+| Prefill parallelism | Interleave CP greater than one; pipeline parallel size one |
+| Attention and KV | TRTLLM DSA prefill/decode, `fp8_e4m3`, page size 64 |
+| DSA indexer | Uncompressed `index_kpool=1`; no cache layer splitting |
+| P/D transfer | Mooncake, with staging buffers disabled |
+| Optional MTP | GLM DSA single-layer NextN, EAGLE, top-k one |
+| Optional CPU HiCache | `cache` mode, `kernel` I/O, `layer_first` or `page_first` |
+
+KV-sharded serving selects the Python radix tree when no tree backend is
+explicitly configured. L3 storage (including runtime attachment), external cache
+linkers, HiSparse and two-batch overlap are unsupported. Prefill CUDA graphs,
+P-side speculative graphs and generic FlashInfer autotuning are disabled for
+this path. Scratch buffers for target and draft are charged against the KV
+memory budget, so the usable cache capacity also depends on context length.
+
+The following single-host example uses GPUs 0–1 for prefill and 2–3 for decode.
+Install the [Mooncake transfer engine](#requirements) first. Both workers use
+intra-node NVLink/CUDA IPC, which supports their ordinary CUDA allocations;
+this is distinct from fabric NVLink, which requires exportable memory.
+For workers on different hosts, configure the appropriate RDMA or fabric
+transport instead of `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK`.
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER=0
+export SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=INTRA_NODE_NVLINK
+export MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK=true
+
+COMMON_ARGS=(
+  --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code
+  --tp-size 2 --context-length 16384 --max-running-requests 1
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3

+  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake
